name: templates-dir-validation
body: Templates dir validation: before any deck validation, render or serve (startup and every reload), kalide validates the resolved library layers — the external library at the configured `templates:` path when the key is set, and the deck-root `templates/` directory when it exists (layered-template-library) — the loader's single resolution and validation point — fail-fast in a fixed order: (1) each layer's `library.yaml` present and valid; (2) each layer's structure (templates-dir-layout: the library structure is library.yaml, slides/, sections/, themes/ and media/, and its template names are unique across slides/ and sections/. Every other top-level entry is ignored — the loader validates only the library itself, so a `.git/` directory, a README, a root-level `AGENTS.md` (library-guide-layout) or any other unrelated entry loads cleanly and stays inert: it is never parsed, validated, rendered, listed or served); (2a) the merged library is unique across layers — a slide name, a section name, a theme name or a `media/` path carried by both layers is a templates error naming the name and both paths (library-layer-uniqueness); (3) each template in kind-then-name order (slides/ then sections/): `template.yaml`, `layout.html.tmpl`, `example.md` present, `template.yaml` well-formed against the schema vocabulary (no `usage:` key), layout parses as standard html/template with the documented function set (template-language), parse errors file:line-qualified; (4) the template-build-checks across the merged set (requirements.constraint.template-registry-integrity); (5) each theme in name order has `theme.css`; (6) references resolve within each layer: in a theme's `theme.css` — and in every stylesheet it reaches through `@import`, wherever in that layer that stylesheet lives (the same theme directory, another theme, or `media/`) — each `@import` directive is followed in either form, the quoted-string form `@import ""x.css"";` and the `url()` form `@import url(""x.css"");`; an `@import` target with no reserved prefix resolves relative to the importing CSS file's own location and must stay inside that file's own tree (its theme directory, or `media/` for a stylesheet imported through `media:`), a `media:` target resolves under that layer's `media/` (the path after the prefix relative to `media/` and staying within it, like a layout `media ""path""` argument), and a `theme:<name>/` target resolves under that layer's theme directory (an unknown `<name>` is a templates error); imports are followed bounded and cycle-safe, with a cycle detected across the whole import graph (including a theme↔media and a theme↔theme cycle); an `@import` target that is a missing file, an absolute path, a `..` leaving the referencing file's own tree, a reference outside the layer, or any other scheme is a templates error naming the offending CSS file and line; in every served stylesheet each relative `url(…)` resolves from that stylesheet's own location to an existing file inside its own tree (its theme directory, or `media/` for a stylesheet imported through `media:`), cross-tree reach being only through `media:` / `theme:<name>/`, and a relative `..` that leaves its own tree is rejected, a `url()` carrying the reserved `media:` prefix resolves to an existing file under that layer's `media/` (relative to `media/` and staying within it) exactly like a layout `media ""path""` argument, and a `url()` carrying the reserved `theme:<name>/` prefix resolves to an existing file inside that layer's theme directory; every other scheme (http:, data:, //, …), an absolute path and a `..` leaving the stylesheet's own tree are rejected with a templates error naming the offending CSS file and line; every relative src/href in a layout resolves to an existing file inside that template's layer; and every `media ""path""` argument in a layout is a relative path inside that layer's `media/` naming an existing file under it — a violation is a templates error qualified with the layout's file:line (requirements.constraint.media-paths-library-relative); (6a) the external layer is self-contained: every section, theme and media reference inside an external-layer template or theme — a `section` helper target name, a `media:`/`theme:<name>/` theme-CSS reference, and a `media ""path""` argument — resolves within the external library alone, so the external library validates on its own, and a reference from an external template or theme to a local-layer section, theme or media name is a templates error, while a local template's `section` helper call resolves against the merged set (library-layer-references); the self-containment rule extends to `{{ template }}` layout composition for the external-to-local direction: a `{{ template }}` call names a library layout by its root-qualified layout name, a call naming a layout its own layer carries resolves within that layer, a local-layer layout's `{{ template ""<external root>/slides|sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl"" . }}` call resolves against the merged library's layout set — the set the local layer's checks and the example run execute against (example-layout-composition, library-layer-references) — and an external-layer layout's `{{ template ""<local root>/slides|sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl"" . }}` call naming a local-layer layout is a templates error, because the external layer validates on its own against a namespace holding only its own layouts; (7) each example.md validates against its template and its layout executes (execute errors file:line-qualified). The first failure is reported as a templates error: path-qualified with the layer root it comes from (e.g. `<root>/slides/content/template.yaml:12`), with a hint and closest-match suggestion where applicable, in the terminal at startup and in the full-page error on reload — the same error-reporting format as deck errors, labelled as a templates error. AC: one test per step shows the expected first error (step 2a includes a slide name, a section name, a theme name and a `media/` path carried by both layers, each rejected naming the name and both paths; step 6 includes a missing `media` file, a `..` argument and an absolute argument; a `media:` theme-CSS reference to a missing file and one with a `..` or absolute path; a `theme:<name>/` reference to an unknown theme and to a missing file; a `..`, absolute path or scheme in either prefixed form; a relative `url('../other/x')` from a theme CSS that leaves its own tree; an `@import` to a missing file, an absolute path or a `..` leaving its own tree; and an `@import` cycle spanning a theme and `media/` or two themes; a clean `@import url('media:css/x.css')` and `@import url('theme:default/theme.css')` validate; step 6a includes an external template referencing a local-only section, which is rejected, and a local template calling an external section, which validates; `{{ template }}` layout composition resolves within a layer and from a local-layer layout to an external-layer layout: a local-layer layout invoking an external-layer layout by its root-qualified layout name resolves, and an external-layer layout invoking a local-layer layout by its root-qualified layout name is a templates error); a valid pair of layers proceeds to deck validation.
